title: Shared Signals Framework
heading: Shared Signals — a transmitter lives here
sub: OpenID SSF 1.0 (final, 2 September 2025) over RFC 8417 Security Event Tokens, RFC 9493 subject identifiers, and RFC 8935 / 8936 delivery. The issuer is {issuer}.
off: Turned off (ssf.enabled) — every endpoint but the metadata answers 501.
notAnEndpoint: This page is not an SSF endpoint; a real transmitter publishes nothing like it.
pipe: SSF is the PIPE and not the vocabulary. It defines how two parties agree a stream, who the events are about, what they travel in and how they get there — and exactly TWO events of its own, both about the pipe. The vocabularies are CAEP (what happened to a session) and RISC (what happened to an account), and neither is here yet. Nothing generates an event on its own: every SET this service transmits was asked for, at the verification endpoint, on {console} or through the management API.
discoveryText: Everything below is published at {metadataUrl}, which is never gated — a receiver has to be able to read what the endpoints are before it can authenticate to one.
name: Name
signing: Every SET is signed with {alg} (ssf.signingAlgorithm), through the same signer every other JWT here goes through — so the post-quantum algorithms are available: ML-DSA at three sizes, SLH-DSA at two, and the six composite ML-DSA + traditional ones. This is the document most worth signing that way: a SET records that something happened and RFC 8417 section 4.1.4 forbids it to expire, so it is read long after it was written.
complex: A complex subject has no format and carries any of {members}, each itself a subject identifier. That is what makes “this session was revoked” expressible: the person is not revoked, one session of theirs is. Critical members here: {critical}.
authOn: SSF 1.0 section 8 requires these endpoints to be protected and has the transmitter PUBLISH what it accepts, in authorization_schemes — so a receiver discovers how to authenticate rather than guessing. It is ON.
authOff: SSF 1.0 section 8 requires these endpoints to be protected and has the transmitter PUBLISH what it accepts, in authorization_schemes — so a receiver discovers how to authenticate rather than guessing. It is OFF (unreachable since 2026-09-06).
noStreams: No streams. A receiver creates one by POSTing a Stream Configuration to the configuration endpoint above.
doesNotDo: What it deliberately does not do
jwks: the key every SET is signed with
